title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
To strengthen trade unions’ capacity to implement the principle of Convention No. 190, the Central Organization of Trade Unions in Kenya, adopted in August 2023, guidelines to their affiliates on how to prevent and address sexual and gender-based harassment in the world of work. The Guidelines were developed as a key measure to implement Convention No. 190 and Recommendation No. 206, through a consultative and consensus building process with government, employers, and other social partners. The Guidelines were also developed using key informant interviews to include perspectives from the government, employers, unions, UN agencies and civil society organizations which were then consolidated to provide a framework for prevention and response to Gender Based Violence and Sexual Harassment (GBV/SH) at the workplace. The Guidelines were validated by COTU(K) in August 2023 ready for national roll out.
To strengthen national efforts towards eliminating violence and harassment in the world of work in Kenya, COTU-K embarked on an Convention No. 190 ratification advocacy campaign, including meetings with several stakeholders such as the Government, the women league within COTU-K, National assembly, and the Senate. Through this campaign, COTU-K and their workers’ structure submitted a memorandum for the ratification of Convention No. 190 to the National assembly and the Senate. Through COTU-K’s advocacy campaign, the President of Kenya committed during the labour day to ensure that Kenya ratifies Convention No. 190.
Additionally, COTU-K was able to work through the women league to develop a model clause which has been adopted and used in the negotiation of the CBAs. With the support of GLO/23/01/UNA; Country envelopes 2023 global project Accelerating progress on HIV and AIDS and ending inequalities in the world of work, the ILO supported the Central Organization of Trade Unions in Kenya from October 2022, to develop guidelines to address sexual and gender-based violence at the workplace, a key measure for implementation of C190 and R206 in the world of work. The ILO provided technical assistance in drafting the guidelines and facilitated consultations with social partners.. The ILO further supported key informant interviews with government, employers, unions, UN agencies and civil society organizations, which contributed to the development of the Guidelines. The United States Department of Labor (USDOL) funded "Strengthening Capacity of Governments to Address Child Labour and Forced Labour, Violations of Acceptable Conditions of Work Project" (RAF/19/09/USA), availed additional resources for the ILO support to COTU-K to conduct an advocacy campaign on the ILO Convention Number 190 with a purpose to support its ratification.
